question: An operations lead runs a project whose instructions describe the team's standard weekly status report. This week only, a board member has asked for a one-page version. What is the best way to handle the request?
options: A) Create a second project duplicating the same knowledge base but with one-page reports as its house rule.
B) Add a permanent line to the project instructions saying every status report must be exactly one page long.
C) Ask for the one-page version in that chat, leaving the project instructions describing the normal report.
D) Upload the board member's request into project knowledge so Claude applies the shorter format from now on.
correct_answers: C) Ask for the one-page version in that chat, leaving the project instructions describing the normal report.
explanations: A whole parallel workspace is heavy maintenance for a single request, and the two projects will drift apart.
Baking a one-off requirement into durable direction changes every future report for a single exception.
Correct. A one-off need belongs in the individual request; durable instructions should keep describing the standing format.
Knowledge is background material, not direction, and this still makes a temporary need permanent.
